concept.name: Docker Images & Layers

relationships.description: Connects Docker Images & Layers to canary deployments in the broader engineering catalog.

concept.tagline: Immutable SHA-256 content-addressable filesystem layers merged by OverlayFS, optimized via BuildKit DAG caching and multi-stage distroless builds.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of OCI/Docker image layers—from OverlayFS lowerdir/upperdir and whiteout bloat to BuildKit cache/secret mounts and multi-stage builds.

spark.summary: A Docker image is an immutable stack of content-addressable filesystem tarballs (layers) merged at runtime via a copy-on-write union filesystem like OverlayFS.
spark.keyTakeaway: Order Dockerfile instructions from least-frequently changed to most-frequently changed, combine `RUN` cleanup in the same layer, and use multi-stage builds so build toolchains never ship to production.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** An OCI/Docker image is a JSON manifest pointing to an ordered stack of immutable, compressed filesystem tarballs (**layers**), each capturing the delta of one `RUN`, `COPY`, or `ADD` instruction by its SHA-256 digest.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Read-Only SHA-256 Lower Layers Merged with Writable Upperdir (lowerdir: Base OS -> lowerdir: App Deps -> upperdir (CoW) -> merged /rootfs); Multi-Stage Go Build + Registry Digest Deduplication (Repo + .dockerignore -> Builder Stage -> Distroless Stage -> OCI Registry).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Pick the smallest base image compatible with your runtime's libc and debugging requirements. Keep layer counts well below ~125 (avoiding OverlayFS lookup degradation), avoid unpacking 100k+ tiny files that exhaust host `ext4`/`xfs` inodes, and pair multi-stage distroless.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Connect Docker layer hygiene with container image scanning, Kubernetes OOM/CrashLoopBackOff debugging, and serverless cold starts.

learningJourney.title: What are Docker Images, Layers & OverlayFS
learningJourney.explanation:
An OCI/Docker image is a JSON manifest pointing to an ordered stack of immutable, compressed filesystem tarballs (**layers**), each capturing the delta of one `RUN`, `COPY`, or `ADD` instruction by its SHA-256 digest.

At startup, `containerd` + `runc` instruct Linux **OverlayFS** to mount the read-only image layers as `lowerdir`, attach a container-writable `upperdir`, and expose the unified view at `merged`. Ten containers on one host share a single physical copy of the base layers in page cache.

sectionDiagram.title: Read-Only SHA-256 Lower Layers Merged with Writable Upperdir
sectionDiagram.summary: Lower layers are immutable and shared across pods; deleting a lower-layer file only writes a .wh.<file> whiteout in upperdir.

learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Docker Images, Layers & OverlayFS works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why Poor Layer Hygiene Bloats Images & Busts CI Caches
learningJourney.explanation: BuildKit evaluates cache top-down: `COPY . .` before `pip install` or `npm ci` invalidates dependency layers on every `README.md` edit. Meanwhile, running `RUN rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` or `RUN rm .npmrc` in a *subsequent* layer only adds a `.wh.*` whiteout—leaving the 38 MB cache or leaked `.npmrc` token permanently extractable in the earlier layer.

sectionDiagram.title: Multi-Stage Go Build + Registry Digest Deduplication
sectionDiagram.summary: Separating build toolchains into AS builder and using cache mounts drops CI rebuilds from minutes to seconds.

ideas.title: FastAPI Slimmed from 1.02 GB to 168 MB (9s CI)
ideas.description: Moving `COPY requirements.txt .` before `pip install --mount=type=cache` and copying the virtualenv into `python:3.12-slim` cut image size 6x and CI build time from 4 min to 9s.

ideas.title: Eliminating Leaked .npmrc Credentials
ideas.description: Replacing `COPY .npmrc` + `RUN rm .npmrc` with `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc` exposed credentials only during that step, leaving zero trace in layer tarballs.

learningJourney.title: Where Layer Optimization Matters (and What Never Belongs in Layers)
learningJourney.explanation: Optimize layers for microservices and multi-arch (`amd64`/`arm64`) OCI distribution; keep mutable DB files and secrets out of image layers.

benefits: Maximizes BuildKit cache hits, speeds K8s node pulls, and removes compiler CVEs.
costs: Distroless lacks `sh`/`curl`—use `kubectl debug` ephemeral containers for live debugging.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Mutable DBs / Heavy Writes in `lowerdir`
benefits: Mount `-v` or `emptyDir`/`PVC` volumes so writes bypass OverlayFS copy-up.
costs: Mutating a 200 MB pre-seeded file in `lowerdir` forces OverlayFS to synchronously copy all 200 MB to `upperdir`.

benefits: Use BuildKit `--mount=type=secret` at build time and K8s Secrets/Vault at runtime.
costs: Anything `COPY`ed—even if later `rm`'d—remains readable in `docker history` and layer blobs.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: How to Write Clean Dockerfiles & Audit Layers with `dive`
learningJourney.explanation:
1. **Strict `.dockerignore`**: Exclude `.git`, `.env*`, `node_modules`, `target/`, and `__pycache__`.
2. **Pin Base Digests**: Use `FROM node:20.18.0-slim@sha256:...` to prevent floating `:latest` drift.
3. **Single-RUN Cleanup & Non-Root**: Chain `apt-get update && ... && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` in one `RUN`, and run as `USER 65532:65532`.
4. **Audit Efficiency**: Run `CI=true dive <image>` (aim for `>95%` efficiency) and scan the final runtime stage with `trivy`.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
FROM golang:1.23-alpine@sha256:c10e7a2b AS builder
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod go mod download
COPY . .
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o /out/server ./cmd/server

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot
USER 65532:65532
COPY --from=builder --chown=65532:65532 /out/server /server
ENTRYPOINT ["/server"]
```

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Full OS vs. Slim vs. Alpine vs. Distroless & Squashing
learningJourney.explanation: Pick the smallest base image compatible with your runtime's libc and debugging requirements.

benefits: Zero shell, zero package manager, minimal CVE surface—ideal for Go/Rust/Java.
costs: No `sh` for `kubectl exec`; requires ephemeral `kubectl debug` containers.

benefits: Full `glibc` compatibility for Python C-extensions/wheels without Alpine `musl` quirks.
Tiny footprint with `apk` available when needed.
costs: `musl` libc can cause DNS quirks and slow Python wheel source builds.

benefits: Collapses whiteouts into one compact tar.
costs: Destroys shared base-layer deduplication across services in the registry.

knowledgeCheck.question: A Dockerfile copies `.npmrc` in layer 3, runs `npm ci` in layer 4, and runs `RUN rm /root/.npmrc` in layer 5. Why is the `.npmrc` secret still compromised?

options.text: `RUN rm` in layer 5 only writes a `.wh..npmrc` whiteout marker in OverlayFS; the original `.npmrc` bytes remain extractable in layer 3. Use `RUN --mount=type=secret` instead
options.feedback: Correct: OCI layers are immutable—later `RUN rm` instructions never shrink or scrub earlier layers.
OverlayFS hides the file in the merged view via a whiteout, but the lower layer tarball stays intact.

options.text: Adding `.npmrc` to `.dockerignore` while still `COPY`ing it fixes the leak
options.feedback: If `.npmrc` is in `.dockerignore`, `COPY .npmrc` fails; `--mount=type=secret` is the BuildKit solution.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
